newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCC rates sag, especially for older ships.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCC rates sag, especially for older ships.

text.p: Very large crude carrier (VLCC) rates from the Middle East, which have recently hit year highs, fell on Thursday as enquiry drained away, brokers said.
"In the last couple of weeks only a few VLCCs have been fixed...Rates are definitely coming off," one broker said.
He said Thailand's PTT had been holding out for as low as W60 for a two-million-barrel vessel, but he did not expect rates to sink that low for now.
"There is a bigger gap now between older and modern tonnage...By next week rates will all be down in the 60s," he added.

Brokers said the current rate for a modern ship to Japan or South Korea was around W70/72.5, down from the recent year high of W75, while older ships to other eastern destinations might not fetch more than W65.

But West Africa/east VLCCs were holding up with vessels fixed at W62.5 on good enquiry, although to the U.S. Gulf they were sagging at W62.5. "VLs are definitely firmer in the west than they are in the east," another broker said.

In the Mediterranean, 80,000 tonne vessels (Aframaxes) edged up to W120 from W117.5, and in the north Aframaxes were also firm at around W130. "There are quite a good number of cargoes and only a few vessels in the Med," an Italian broker said.
Med Suezmaxes (130,000 tonne ships), meanwhile, were steady at about W92.5.
Western hemisphere rates were little changed, with 70,000 tonne crude cargoes at W175 and 50,000 tonne fuel oil stems at W195, brokers said. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
